text_body: SEATTLE SEAHAWKS Instant reaction to Seattle Seahawks’ 17-13 loss to 49ers Sep 7, 2025, 4:23 PM | Updated: 6:14 pm Instant Reaction: #Seahawks vs. #49ers Week 1 Seahawks broadcaster Dave Wyman (Wyman & Bob) shares his takeaways from the Seahawks week 1 loss vs NFC West rival SF 49ers from Lumen Field on September 7, 2025. For a full game recap & more analysis, visit SeattleSports.com. 0 seconds of 0 seconds Volume 0% Press shift question mark to access a list of keyboard shortcuts Keyboard Shortcuts Enabled Disabled Shortcuts Open/Close / or ? Play/Pause SPACE Increase Volume ↑ Decrease Volume ↓ Seek Forward → Seek Backward ← Captions On/Off c Fullscreen/Exit Fullscreen f Mute/Unmute m Decrease Caption Size - Increase Caption Size + or = Seek % 0-9 0.5x 1x 1.25x 1.5x 2x facebook x Email Link https://sports.mynorthwest.com/nfl/seattle-seahawks/instant-reaction-seattle-seahawks-17-13-loss-49ers/1821418 Copied Loading ad Live 00:25 00:00 02:45 BY SEATTLESPORTS.COM STAFF Staff report The Seattle Seahawks came up short down the stretch in their season opener, giving up a late touchdown and losing a fumble on their final drive to fall 17-13 to the NFC West rival San Francisco 49ers. Recap | Observations | What we learned | Box score You can watch Seahawks analyst, Wyman and Bob host and former NFL linebacker Dave Wyman break down his reaction in the video at the top of this post. Below, here’s what some other voices of Seattle Sports have to say about the Week 1 loss. Mike Salk – Brock and Salk (6-10 a.m. weekdays) It’s amazing how often the same things pop up for the same people at the biggest moments. Riq Woolen has all the ability in the world, but twice he got greedy on the final Niners’ drive, and twice it came back to bite them. Purdy making magic happen 🪄 Jake Tonges with the hands 🙌 📺: FOX NFL+ // https://t.co/KTh0i4oaLh pic.twitter.com/26IBNBe9MT — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) September 7, 2025 Sam Darnold has had fumble issues at crucial points of games going all the way back to his time at USC, and losing a ball inside the opposing red zone with the game on the line would certainly fit inside the category of “crucial.” 🐻🐻🐻 📺: FOX NFL+ // https://t.co/KTh0i4oaLh pic.twitter.com/pC6aXVFZ3O — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) September 7, 2025 There were some real positives for the Seahawks in their first game of the season. But that’s a preventable loss to a beat up and beatable San Francisco team. Plenty to clean up before a long trip to Pittsburgh next Sunday. Mike Lefko – Wyman and Bob (2-7 p.m.) I think we knew there would be growing pains with this offense, but that was an uninspired, ugly display for nearly all of the second half. Way too many screen passes and too much of trying to alternate Kenneth Walker III in with Zach Charbonnet at running back. It feels like Charbonnet is indeed better equipped to be the featured back in this offense as the season goes along. ‘Not the start that we wanted’ for Seahawks’ offense Outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, there also wasn’t much of a receiving threat that emerged. Maybe that’s Darnold comfort level with JSN or receivers weren’t able to win matchups, but the lack of a secondary receiving option looms large right now. Someone hit rewind. 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/Jwb6at6Dm3 — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) September 7, 2025 The Seahawks’ defense kept them in it for most of the game but unfortunately Riq Woolen had two absolutely critical lapses at the worst time. The prevailing notion from the national media about the Seahawks is that the rest of the division got better while the Seahawks have a lot of question marks to iron out at key positions. That certainly looks to be the case after our small sample of Week 1. Brock Huard – Brock and Salk I hate that Seahawk loss So much incredible want to by so many, but absolute lack of focus & finish by a few dismantles the effort That’s a game you gotta have — Brock Huard (@BrockHuard) September 7, 2025 Injury Update: Latest on Seahawks rookie safety Emmanwori

Jan 05, 2026 at 11:15 AM New Orleans Saints Copied! Michael C. Hebert/New Orleans Saints The New Orleans Saints finished the season 6-11, in fourth place in the NFC South, in Kellen Moore's first year as head coach of the Saints. The team started the season with quarterback Spencer Rattler as the starter getting out to a 1-7 start through Week 8. The team then handed the keys to rookie quarterback Tyler Shough and finished the remainder of the season 5-4. Here's a game-by-game breakdown of the Saints' 2025 NFL season. Saints vs. Cardinals | 2025 NFL Week 1 WHEN/WHERE: Sept. 7, 2025 at Caesars Superdome, New Orleans, LA RESULT: Cardinals 20, Saints 13 RECORD: (0-1) 🏈 GAME RECAP | 📸 GAME PHOTOS | 🎥 GAME HIGHLIGHTS | 📝 GAME NOTES GAME SUMMARY A few big plays from the Arizona Cardinals and a slew of penalties by the New Orleans Saints led to a 20-13 Arizona victory in Sunday's season-opener at the Caesars Superdome. The game marked the debut of Coach Kellen Moore and it ended a streak of six consecutive opening game victories for the Saints. New Orleans had a chance to tie the score but its final possession end with an incompletion on fourth-and-10 from the 18-yard line. FULL GAME RECAP GAME NOTES & STATS New Orleans outgained Arizona in yards 315-276. The Saints had 208 net passing yards and 107 rushing yards. The Saints had 21 first downs compared to Arizona's 19. Running back Alvin Kamara led the backfield with 45 yards on 11 rushes and one 18-yard rushing touchdown. He also had two catches for 12 yards. With Kamara's 45 rushing yards, he surpasses Wilbert Montgomery and Robert Smith for 75th all-time (6,824) in NFL record books, and his 12 receiving yards passes LaDainian Tomlinson for 13th all-time for running backs (4,774). Kamara's touchdown in the second quarter was the 1,000th by the team in the Caesars Superdome regular season and postseason combined since 1975. The Saints are the third team all-time to do it, joining the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field (1,114 prior to Green Bay's late afternoon game) and the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium (1,029). The Buffalo Bills have 998 at Highmark Stadium. Defensive end Cameron Jordan finished with three tackles, including 1.5 sacks for 14.5 yards, two stops for loss and one pass deflection. Jordan now has 123 career sacks, surpassing Clyde Simmons and Simeon Rice, and tying Robert Mathis for 20th all-time in NFL record books. This was his first time throwing multiple touchdowns in a game in his career. He also rushed four times for 14 yards. Running back Alvin Kamara recorded 99 rushing yards, surpassing Curt Warner, Antowain Smith and Rodney Hampton to be 72nd all-time in NFL record books. He also caught six passes for 21 yards. It was the first victory of Coach Kellen Moore's tenure and the first win for Spencer Rattler as the team's starting quarterback as the Saints improved to 1-4. The loss dropped the Giants to 1-4. Recap | Instant reaction | What we learned | Box score What stood out from the defeat? Here are some observations. Ugly debut for new-look offense Simply put, it was not a good start for Seattle’s revamped offense under new coordinator Klint Kubiak. After showing promise in the preseason, the Seahawks’ ground attack sputtered much like it did for most of last year. Seattle rushed for just 84 yards on 26 carries – with running backs Zach Charbonnet and Kenneth Walker III combining for just 67 yards on 22 carries. The passing game was similarly unspectacular, and extremely one-dimensional. Sam Darnold threw for just 150 yards in his Seahawks debut, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba accounting for nearly all of that production with nine catches for 124 yards. The rest of Seattle’s pass catchers mustered just seven receptions for 26 yards. ‘Not the start that we wanted’ for Seahawks’ offense The play-calling also was curious at times, as many staples of Kubiak’s Shanahan-style scheme – wide-zone blocking, under-center passing, play-action bootlegs – were seemingly underutilized. It felt like the game plan strayed a bit too far from this offense’s core identity, which perhaps was intended as a curveball due to the strong schematic and coaching ties between Kubiak and 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan. Either way, the end result was not good: 13 points and 230 total yards. And it certainly won’t do anything to quiet the naysayers who doubted and questioned Seattle’s offseason overhaul on this side of the ball. Late turnovers prove costly For most of the afternoon, Seattle’s offense avoided the big mistake. But over the final 15 minutes, the Seahawks committed a pair of costly turnovers that ultimately did them in. On the opening snap of the fourth quarter, Seattle had the ball in San Francisco territory when Smith-Njigba lost a fumble on a short completion, squashing an opportunity for the Seahawks to extend a three-point lead. And in the game’s closing moments, with Seattle inside the San Francisco 10-yard line and Darnold seemingly on the precipice of channeling more of his 2024 late-game magic, disaster struck. Edge rusher Nick Bosa overpowered right tackle Abraham Lucas and pushed him into Darnold’s arm, causing a strip-sack fumble that Bosa fell on to seal the game. Overall, the Seahawks’ offensive line actually held up quite well in pass protection. But in the game’s most crucial moment, one of the league’s premier game-wreckers had his way. NICK BOSA CALLS GAME SFvsSEA on FOX https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/7cck4psHjo — NFL (@NFL) September 7, 2025 More up-and-down play from Woolen The first few seasons of cornerback Riq Woolen’s NFL career have been marked by maddening inconsistencies, with flashes of tantalizing potential overshadowed at times by head-scratching mistakes. That was once again the case on Sunday. With just under 10 minutes to play, Woolen showed the best of his unique skill set, using his blazing speed and lengthy 6-foot-4 frame to make an impressive pass breakup at the pylon that helped limit the 49ers to a field goal. But in the game’s final minutes, Woolen misplayed a pair of passes on San Francisco’s deciding touchdown drive. The first came on a deep sideline pass where Woolen seemed to be in prime position for a pass breakup, but then appeared to misjudge the ball and slow down, which allowed wide receiver Ricky Pearsall to get behind him for a key 45-yard completion. And then shortly after that, with the 49ers facing a third-and-3 from the 4-yard line, Woolen again appeared to be in good position to make a play. But instead, third-string tight end Jake Tonges beat Woolen to the spot and hauled in an end-zone jump ball for what proved to be the winning score. Woolen’s two late gaffes overshadowed a gutsy performance from Seattle’s defense, which had allowed just 10 points on four red-zone trips prior to that final touchdown drive. text_body: Xtra Points Steelers drop home opener to Seahawks, 31-17 Sep 14, 2025 at 05:45 PM Jim Wexell Correspondent Copied! Gamebook The Seattle Seahawks outscored the Steelers 17-3 in the fourth quarter en route to a 31-17 win at Acrisure Stadium. "Certainly a disappointing home opener," said Coach Mike Tomlin. "There's a lot of things that we can do better in all phases and in coaching and we will." The Steelers led 14-7 at the half, but the visitors were able to even the score early in the third quarter through a 10-play, 80-yard touchdown scoring drive and seized the lead for good with a 55-yard field goal by kicker Jason Myers with 12:46 left in the quarter. On the ensuing kickoff, the ball got past rookie Kaleb Johnson and landed in the endzone. Seattle's George Holani pounced on the ball for a touchdown, giving the Seahawks a 24-14 lead with 12:46 remaining. "Poor judgement by a young player," said Tomlin after the game. For three-plus quarters, the game was a tight struggle. The Seahawks opened the scoring with a 21-yard touchdown pass from Sam Darnold to Tory Horton to cap the game's opening drive. The Steelers answered with a 48-yard Chris Boswell field goal to cut the deficit to 7-3. A pair of third-down conversions aided the drive, the first on a defensive hold and the other a 9-yard draw by Jaylen Warren. An incompletion on third-and-2 brought out Boswell for his first of three field goals on the day. Seahawks score bizarre TD on kickoff to beat Steelers Sam Darnold passed for 295 yards and two touchdowns, overcoming a pair of first-half interceptions. Only the two early picks by Darnold allowed the Steelers to hang around. DK Metcalf caught three passes for 20 yards, including a 2-yard touchdown, but was largely a non-factor against his former team. Jaylen Warren ran for 48 yards and caught four passes for 86 more, but the crispness that defined Pittsburgh’s triumph against the Jets vanished against a Seattle defense that didn’t miss a beat, even with starting cornerback Devon Witherspoon sidelined by injury. Holani’s recovery came in almost the same spot where teammate Derion Kendrick picked off Rodgers on a tipped ball late in the third quarter to thwart a potential Steelers scoring drive. text_body: George Holani's 'Crazy' Special Teams Touchdown Help Seahawks Take Control In Win Over Steelers George Holani’s score an unusual touchdown on special teams to spark a 17-point fourth quarter in the Seahawks 31-17 win in Pittsburgh. Sep 14, 2025 at 04:00 PM John Boyle Seahawks.com Senior Reporter Copied! Matt Durisko/Copyright 2025 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. Seattle Seahawks running back George Holani (36) exits the field after an NFL football game, Sunday, Sept. 14, 2025, in Pittsburgh. (AP Photo/Matt Durisko) PITTSBURGH—George Holani could not have possibly envisioned that his first NFL touchdown would happen like it did. It was a touchdown no one saw coming. "One of the more interesting plays that I've seen in my career, but it was just great to see our guy George get into the end zone that way," quarterback Sam Darnold said. "That was crazy," added safety Coby Bryant. "I'm not going to lie, I've never seen nothing like that. But first touchdown in the NFL, so I'm happy for him." That most interesting, crazy play occurred early in the fourth quarter when the Steelers failed to field a short Jason Myers kickoff, which bounced over returner Kaleb Johnson and into the end zone. Johnson, seeming to not realize the ball was still live and had not rolled out of the end zone, didn't go after the ball, allowing Holani to fall on it just before sliding out of the end zone. "I wouldn't have thought I'd score on kickoff, honestly, but I got my first touchdown on special teams, and it's a blessing," Holani said. "We go over situations in our special teams meeting every week. We see teams who always mess up, and we don't want to be that team out there that's looking not good." Describing the play, Holani said, "I knew it was going to be a touchdown as long as I down the ball with possession. I had to run full speed to the end zone, then I had to stop and like cradle, get small and get in there and possess the ball. It was just a heads up play that we took advantage of." The play was not just an unusual one, it was a very consequential one in Seattle's 31-17 win over the Steelers. Moments before that touchdown, the game was tied 14-14, then Myers kicked a field goal to give the Seahawks a three-point lead, setting up what looked at the time to be a close finish. But seconds later, Holani was falling on a loose ball in the end zone, and a game that had just been tied saw the Seahawks leading by 10. "It was a heck of a play by George, understanding the situation, then staying in bounds and recovering it, which actually, (director of football analysis and special situations) Brian Eayrs talked about sideline recoveries yesterday, as a matter of fact, so Brian Eayrs deserves a lot of credit too. But George made a heck of a play." Another key to the play was Myers' short kick, which Johnson was unable to field. "It's tougher than it looks, because the landing zone, it's easy to kick it short of the landing zone, so if you're going to kick it low, you've got to be on your stuff, and he's on his stuff right now," Macdonald said. While there were certainly mistakes and it wasn’t perfect, this Seattle offense really took a nice step forward this week. Sam Darnold had some brilliant plays throughout this game, and more importantly he was able to bounce back from his mistakes, throwing two interceptions in this game. Seeing a more even distribution amongst Darnold’s receivers I think should ease a lot of minds out there. More importantly probably for this team is seeing the running game established the way that it was today with Kenneth Walker III gaining 105 yards and a TD on just 13 carries. Stacy Rost: Seahawks got out of own way, back to identity I think we also saw for the second week in a row that this defense is going to be a problem for opponents in a big way this season. They held the Steelers to 267 total yards on the day. They did that in spite of the offense putting them in bad field position with a couple of turnovers. There are a lot of things to like coming out of this win and certainly reasons to feel decidedly more optimistic about what this team can be this season. Mike Salk – Brock and Salk The Seahawks won by 14 points. It probably could have been a whole lot more. Regardless of the final score, they were the better team this weekend in Pittsburgh and they showed it over 60 minutes. After leaving points on the board in the first half with a missed field goal, a blown fourth-down decision and a pick that set up the Steelers for an early score, they roared to life in the second half. For all the questions about the offensive weaponry, it was the skill players that made a difference. Kenneth Walker was great. His runs on the first drive of the third quarter and the backbreaking third down score in the fourth quarter changed the game. LET'S GOOOOO 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/dy9x8w7hhn — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) September 14, 2025 Sam Darnold did it with his legs and arm. JSN was a constant presence playing at a superstar level (and badly outplaying DK Metcalf). And Cooper Kupp looked like a different player a week after a questionable debut at home. There’s still plenty of work to do. The run game had its concerns and the turnovers need to be curbed. But by winning in Week 2 on the road, the Seahawks opened up the rest of their season and gave themselves a shot to accomplish anything they want. Mike Lefko – Wyman and Bob Despite a couple of shaky drives, the Seahawks’ offense looked really good, especially when it mattered the most. It feels like offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak can script opening drives well, with both possessions to start the half ending in touchdowns. The opening drive was particularly nice after two third-down conversions and a well-designed play to spring Tory Horton for his first career TD reception. Tory Horton breaks Seahawks’ lengthy opening-drive TD drought It was encouraging to see the way Sam Darnold can bounce back in a game. The two interceptions weren’t ideal, but his touchdown drive to start the third quarter was precise, and the third-down play to evade traffic and find AJ Barner in the fourth led to the game-sealing TD run from Ken Walker. The special teams gaffe by the Steelers obviously changed the game, but credit the Seahawks defense – without Devon Witherspoon – for keeping the Steelers’ offense in check for the entire second half. The Seahawks rolled to a 44-13 blowout win over New Orleans at Lumen Field on Sunday after jumping out to a commanding 38-3 lead in the first half. Seattle Seahawks win: Observations | Recap | Box score With the win, the Seahawks improved to 2-1 while getting the chance to rest their regulars in the second half ahead of a Thursday night meeting with NFC West rival Arizona. The Saints, who are coming off a 5-12 season in 2024, fell to 0-3 in their first year under Moore, a former standout quarterback for Prosser High School and Boise State. Check out the instant reactions to the game from the voices of Seattle Sports in this post, including Seahawks Radio Network analyst Dave Wyman’s thoughts in the video at the top. Mike Salk – Brock and Salk (6-10 a.m. weekdays) The Seahawks look like a good team. The Saints appear to be a very bad one. And on this day, that played out exactly as you might have hoped it would. Utter and complete dominance for the Seahawks in a way we haven’t seen in years. Stacy Rost: There’s important context to Seahawks’ runaway win There are plenty of flowers to be handed out after one like this, but I would offer my top game ball to the scouts because this game was won in many ways by the players on the outside margin of the roster. D’Anthony Bell, Chazz Surratt, Derion Kendrick, Josh Jobe, Eric Saubert and Dareke Young all made significant contributions that helped put this one away early. That speaks to the depth of the roster, the way this coaching staff prepares everyone, and the eagle eye of the scouting department in finding some diamonds in the rough. Bob Stelton – Wyman and Bob (2-7 p.m. weekdays) It was hard to tell in this one if the Seahawks are very good or the Saints are a disaster. I think the truth is that it’s a little of both. It’s hard to find something that didn’t go right for the Seahawks today. The stats were not huge but the score was, and they got there by being incredibly efficient. I loved that the Seahawks were aggressive out of the gate and jumped on a team that clearly was involved in a mismatch. The Seahawks did not punt until the third quarter. Sam Darnold looked very sharp with some nice pinpoint throws moving this team up and down the field. Special teams came up huge with Tory Horton and his 95-yard punt return for a touchdown, a blocked punt, and giving this team good field position to work with throughout the majority of the game. The defense going shorthanded today was still absolutely dominant despite playing without Devon Witherspoon, Julian love, and Nick Emmanwori. They forced Saints quarterback Spencer Rattler into his first interception of the season and basically shut down anything the Saints attempted to do with the run or pass. If you want to nitpick to find something that didn’t go well for the Hawks, the run game would be what I think most would point to. They had very little luck in terms of leaning on the rushing attack to eat up clock and pile up yardage, yet Kenneth Walker III had two short-yardage touchdowns and got a bit more effective in the second half. Overall, this was a win they needed on a short week, and they were able to get it done without some crucial starters and even getting to rest some starters in the fourth quarter. Brock Huard – Brock and Salk Mike Macdonald wanted his Seahawks to play complementary ball – that was a master’s class of it. Horton, Darnold, JSN: Spectacular. Byron Murphy II, Josh Jobe, Derion Kendrick: Awesome. The Seahawks’ special teams have been the best in the game, and not having to expend a ton of personnel and snaps in the second half is big deal with the quick turnaround to a Thursday night game this week. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Seattle Sports (@seattlesports710) Mike Lefko – Wyman and Bob A thoroughly impressive win and exactly what you wanted to see against an inferior opponent. For the second straight week, special teams came up with key plays, setting the tone for the Seahawks to bury the Saints before they could even settle into the game. That comfortable margin also allowed the defense to be aggressive, and it’s reassuring they were able to get key contributions from the entire unit with Julian Love and Devon Witherspoon out. The Sam Darnold to Jaxon Smith-Njigba connection continues to grow, and it seems like JSN is well on his way to establishing himself as one of the best receivers in the NFL and certainly a bona fide No. 1 WR on a team. An all-around good win and exactly what you need heading into a short week and a divisional game on Thursday night. Rookie Tory Horton scores longest punt return TD in Seahawks history

title: Saints put on embarrassing display in Week 3 road loss to Seattle
text_body: SAINTS Saints put on embarrassing display in Week 3 road loss to Seattle Bob Rose Saints Wire Sept. 21, 2025, 7:22 p.m. CT After a competitive showing in their first two games despite losses, the New Orleans Saints lost in embarrassing fashion to the Seattle Seahawks on the road. The final score of 44-13 was bad enough, but this game's competitive phase was over after a 21-0 first quarter filled with mistakes and ridiculous blunders that made themselves into a laughing stock. New Orleans drove the ball well enough on their first drive. A poorly thrown deep pass by Spencer Rattler to a wide open Alvin Kamara on a fourth and short gamble turned the ball over on downs. That was immediately followed by a blown sack by Bryan Bresee on Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold that led to a big completion to wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Three plays after that, Bresee handed Seattle another gimme first down on a personal foul penalty to nullify a nice blitz and tipped pass by Isaiah Stalbird that would have forced a field goal. The Seahawks turned those gifts into a touchdown and a 7-0 lead that was a microcosm of the entire first half. An infuriating 95-yard punt return for a touchdown by Tory Horton made it 14-0. A blocked Kai Kroeger punt on the following possession set Seattle up for another easy touchdown and a 21-0 lead. The Saints showed a flickering sign of life with a field goal drive to open the second quarter. Another special teams breakdown on the ensuing kickoff return killed that momentum and handed the Seahawks another easy score for a 28-3 lead. Eight first half penalties, three ridiculous special teams blunders, numerous pass coverage breakdowns, and the inability to block on offense led to a 35-6 halftime deficit. The second half was a prolonged exercise in futility. This was to a Seattle team without three starters in their secondary and Sam Darnold at quarterback. Everyone has an off day, but this one was utterly pathetic. It was only one game, albeit one with humiliating results. But it's back to the drawing board for the Saints, who now face the Buffalo Bills on the road next Sunday. You'd think it couldn't get worse than this catastrophic display, so let's hope we witnessed rock-bottom for the Saints. Seattle Seahawks win: Observations | Reaction | Box score Kenneth Walker III ran for two TDs for the Seahawks (2-1), with the first set up by another big play on special teams. D’Anthony Bell blocked a punt by Kai Kroeger deep in New Orleans territory, and Walker’s 3-yard run gave Seattle a 21-0 first-quarter lead. Horton, who had his first career TD catch a week earlier in a 31-17 win at Pittsburgh, gave the Seahawks a 14-0 lead with his punt return midway through the first quarter. Early the second, Horton hauled in a 14-yard fade from Darnold to put Seattle ahead 28-3. Said it once, we'll say it again. Tory Horton hype train. 🚂 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/Lfo0etftoa — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) September 21, 2025 The Seahawks didn’t let up. Walker’s second short TD run capped a four-play, 76-yard drive that made it 35-3, and Jason Myers added a 56-yard field goal before halftime. Seattle led 38-6 at the break for the second-highest-scoring half in franchise history. For the Saints, it was the most points allowed in a half since they also gave up 38 in the second half of a 62-7 loss to Atlanta on Sept. 16, 1973. Stacy Rost: There’s important context to Seahawks’ runaway win After opening the season with two straight one-score losses, first-year coach Kellen Moore’s Saints (0-3) were overwhelmed at Lumen Field. New Orleans did not reach the end zone until the beginning of the fourth quarter, when Spencer Rattler found backup tight end Jack Stoll for a 13-yard touchdown. The second-year quarterback fell to 0-9 as a starter, and the Saints lost their seventh straight dating to last season. He threw for 218 yards with one interception. Bell’s blocked put ended a streak of 233 straight regular-season games for the Saints without allowing one, the second-longest streak since at least 1960. Seattle’s Jaxon Smith-Njigba had five catches for 96 yards and a score, and Darnold was an efficient 14 of 18 for 218 yards, finishing with a QB rating of 154.2. Injuries Saints safety Justin Reid was evaluated for a concussion in the first half but returned. Seahawks All-Pro cornerback Devon Witherspoon did not play. Safeties Julian Love and Nick Emmanwori and running back Zach Charbonnet also sat out. Up next Saints: Visit Buffalo next Sunday. Seahawks: Visit Arizona next Sunday. text_body: Recap Box Score Expert Picks Plays Analysis StubHub Drive Chart SEA ARI Jason Myers boots 52-yard FG on final play, lifting Seahawks to 23-20 win over Cardinals AP Sep 26, 2025 Learn More GLENDALE, Ariz. (AP) The Seattle Seahawks could have been shell-shocked, giving up a 14-point lead during the latter half of the fourth quarter and turning their comfortable advantage into a tie game with 33 seconds left. It looked like they might need overtime to make amends. Sam Darnold, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Jason Myers had other ideas. Darnold hit Smith-Njigba for a 22-yard gain in a last-minute response, Myers made a 52-yard field goal as time expired, and the Seahawks withstood a late rally by Kyler Murray and the Arizona Cardinals to beat Arizona 23-20 on Thursday night. “I had no doubt we were going to go down there and score, honestly,” Smith-Njigba said. “We just needed one play, a couple plays and Jason's going to go down there and seal the deal.” Seattle has won eight straight over Arizona, its NFC West rival. The Cardinals trailed 20-6 midway through the fourth. Murray threw a 16-yard touchdown pass to Marvin Harrison Jr. that cut the deficit to 20-13 with 5:50 left. After Myers missed a 53-yard field-goal attempt, Murray put together another drive and found Emari Demercado for a 7-yard touchdown with 33 seconds left. But the Seahawks (3-1) weren't done. A penalty on the ensuing kickoff - Chad Ryland's kick landed short of the landing zone - gave Seattle good field position at the 40. Darnold then hit Smith-Njigba for the big gain that moved Seattle into field-goal range. Two plays later, Myers calmly knocked the 52-yarder through, making up for his miss just a few minutes before. “I've seen this guy play golf - he's a stud,” Seattle coach Mike Macdonald said. “He's got ice in his veins. We knew he was going to make that kick.” Said Myers: “I didn't try to change anything - just stay true to my routine. That's what I prepare for during the offseason and all week. Just trusting it and letting it rip." Darnold had another efficient outing, completing 18 of 26 passes for 242 yards and a touchdown. Kenneth Walker III ran for 81 yards and Zach Charbonnet added his second rushing touchdown of the season. The Seahawks' defense sacked Kyler Murray six times. “Sam's playing out of his mind right now,” Macdonald said. “You see him, and he's such a cool customer.” Charbonnet scored on a 1-yard run late in the second quarter, using a second effort to fall into the end zone and give the Seahawks a 14-3 lead heading into halftime. The Cardinals (2-2) jogged to the locker room amid scattered boos from the home crowd. Arizona has struggled on offense most of the season and Thursday was a slog until the fourth quarter. The Cardinals have dropped two straight. “We’ve got to show up and be ready to go,” Murray said. “It’s just taking too long. Obviously, the resilience of the team, you love to see it. You feel like you give yourself a chance to win the game at the end. “But it’s just too late.” Murray completed 27 of 41 passes for 200 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions, though at least one wasn't his fault. Harrison had a rough start to the game before making his touchdown grab in the fourth quarter. Last year's No. 4 overall pick bobbled a ball on a slant route in the second quarter, essentially tossing it to Seattle's Ernest Jones IV, who grabbed it for an interception. It was the second straight walk-off loss for the Cardinals, who fell 16-15 to the 49ers on a last-second field goal just five days earlier. It was the first time since at least 1988 that the Cardinals have lost two games in a row on the final play of regulation, according to Sportradar. “I appreciate the resiliency, that's there,” coach Jonathan Gannon said. “No one has their head down. Everyone believes we can win. But we're not doing enough, all three phases, to win these games. That's very clear.” The Seahawks took a 7-3 lead late in the first quarter on Darnold's 16-yard touchdown pass to AJ Barner. Arizona took a 3-0 lead on Ryland's 33-yard field goal with 4:37 left in the first quarter. The Cardinals grabbed the early advantage partially because of a strange play a few minutes earlier that included turnovers by both teams. Murray threw a ball that was intercepted by Seattle's Coby Bryant, but Bryant fumbled a few seconds later and the ball was recovered by Arizona's Trey Benson at essentially the same spot where the play started. Seattle Seahawks win: Observations | Recap | Box score Playing in a short week on the road against a division rival, the Seahawks let a 14-point lead slip away in the fourth quarter but won 23-20 on a last-second, 52-yard field goal from Jason Myers against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona. Seattle improved to 3-1 on the season and evened its record to 1-1 against division foes. It also extended its winning streak over the Cardinals to eight games. Arizona, which has now last both of its NFC West games, dropped to 2-2. Check out the instant reactions to the game from the voices of Seattle Sports in this post, which includes Seahawks Radio Network analyst Dave Wyman’s thoughts in the video at the top. Mike Salk – Brock and Salk (6-10 a.m. weekdays) I’m starting to really like this Seahawks team. They aren’t perfect, and they showed some of those flaws in Arizona. But Thursday night games tend to be sloppy and it’s up to the players to will their way to victory, and that is exactly what they did. They were the better team, the better offense and the better defense. And while they shot themselves in the foot a few times (Kenneth Walker III’s taunting, Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s hold, and Riq Woolen’s general existence come to mind), they found a way to be better in the biggest moments. I like that they are tough. They are physical. They have old-school elements. They generate real pressure largely without having to blitz. But for a team with those qualities, they also are explosive. We’ll see what that ultimately looks like as they make their way through this season. But at the moment, they are more fun to watch than any of their recent predecessors. And they are starting to build some confidence in themselves, which could pay real dividends down the stretch. Brock Huard – Brock and Salk A game really that Seattle dominated. For 3 1/2 quarters, they were the better team. Everything showed that. The explosives showed it, the yards showed it, the third-down conversions showed it. But credit to Marvin Harrison Jr., who’s been really abysmal for the Cardinals, to step up and rise up and beat Witherspoon multiple times. Credit to attacking Woolen in some one-on-one situations to beat fourth-down blitzes and third-down blitzes and make things interesting. But ultimately, I don’t know how you watch this game and not start thinking of Sam Darnold, of what he was for the majority of the Minnesota season a year ago. He was phenomenal. He was an MVP candidate for the Vikings for 15 weeks last year. Rost: Interesting question emerging about Seattle Seahawks QB And through four weeks of this season, he’s one of the five, ten best quarterbacks – certainly 10 best. The numbers will show you he’s one of the five best quarterbacks in the game. He’s not making mistakes. He’s throwing the ball incredibly accurately. He’s getting the ball out of his hands. He’s creating a sense of belief in everyone around him. Sam leading that game-winning drive when it mattered, that’s what quarterback is all about in the league. And 3-1 for these guys is pretty darn good. "Sam leading that game-winning drive when it mattered, that's what QB is all about in the NFL." @BrockHuard shares his instant reaction to the Seahawks 23-20 win over the Arizona Cardinals. pic.twitter.com/uOFifDHEvl — Seattle Sports (@SeattleSports) September 26, 2025 Mike Lefko – Wyman and Bob (2-7 p.m. weekdays) Well…it was a win. A rough fourth quarter undid what should have been a very impressive and suffocating performance by the defense. Little mistakes, like a holding penalty to undo a TD, a missed field goal and a fumble after an interception came back to almost haunt the Seahawks. The Cardinals couldn’t do anything offensively for most of the night as the interior of the Seahawks defensive line continued to show why they have been one of the best groups in the league this season, but it almost felt like a collective relaxing and rare let down from that group after the Seahawks took a 20-6 lead in the fourth. On the offensive side, it is incredibly encouraging to see the versatility in the passing game for the Seahawks on display. The Cardinals bracketed Jaxon Smith-Njigba all night and removed him as a receiving option, yet the play calling from Kubiak and poise from Darnold helped pivot into a balanced, collective effort. We’re starting to see the emergence of the tight ends in the offense and flashes of why Elijah Arroyo drew such acclaim in the draft. It is exciting to think about what’s possible through the air with this full arsenal of weapons. It was also great to see Darnold lead two drives down the field in the fourth, including the big third-down throw to Smith-Njigba on the drive that preceded their game-winning field goal march. At some point in his Seahawks career, they will need him to do that again, and it felt like that erased a lot of pre-conceived doubts that may have hung over the start of his career here. The run game is very much a work in progress. It feels like they are still trying to find their identity when it comes to utilizing both running backs and when they want to try and run out of the shotgun. That needs to be smoothed out and could become problematic down the road in situations like tonight where the Seahawks needed to put together a long drive to salt away the game after the Cardinals cut it to a one-possession game. Ultimately, it’s a division win on a short week, and that’s all that matters. Seattle Seahawks Roster Moves: Rookie FB Robbie Ouzts placed on IR

After the Seahawks blew a 14-point fourth-quarter lead, Jason Myers made up for an earlier missed field goal by hitting a game-winning 52-yarder as time expired to give Seattle a 23-20 road win over the NFC West rival Arizona Cardinals on Thursday night. Seattle Seahawks win: Recap | Box score It was the Seahawks’ eighth consecutive win over Arizona. It also improved them to 11-1-1 against the Cardinals in State Farm Stadium since 2013. More importantly, Seattle moved to 3-1 on the season with its third straight victory. Here are a few observations from the Seahawks’ last-second triumph. Darnold, JSN come through in the clutch Jaxon Smith-Njigba entered the night as the NFL’s second-leading receiver. But for most of the game, it was a quiet evening for the Seahawks wideout, who didn’t get his first catch until the final minute of the third quarter. But when Seattle needed a big play late, Sam Darnold and Smith-Njigba delivered. After the Cardinals rallied to tie the game at 20-20 with 28 seconds to go, the Seahawks got a break when Arizona’s ensuing kickoff fell just short of the landing zone, resulting in a penalty that set up Seattle on its own 40-yard line. Two plays later, Darnold lofted a back-shoulder pass to Smith-Njigba, who hauled it in for a 22-yard reception that set up Myers’ game-winner. Darnold 🎯 JSN The @seahawks looking to win it. SEAvsAZ on Prime Video Also streaming on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mCvcq1TCRc — NFL (@NFL) September 26, 2025 Darnold and Smith-Njigba also had another big connection just a few minutes earlier. Facing a third-and-6 with their team clinging to a seven-point lead, Darnold hit Smith-Njigba on a well-executed stutter-and-go route for a 36-yard completion to the Arizona 38. That could have helped seal the victory for Seattle, but Myers proceeded to miss a 53-yard field goal, which kept the door ajar for the Cardinals. It was another sharp and decisive performance by Darnold, who finished 18-of-26 passing for 242 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. In addition to his late heroics, he also had an impressive two-play sequence in the first half. Backed up on his own 10-yard line, Darnold escaped the pocket and lofted a 32-yard completion to rookie tight end Elijah Arroyo, and then scrambled for a 24-yard gain on the next play to help spark a 90-yard TD drive. Smith-Njigba, meanwhile, finished four catches for 79 yards. That bumped his season total to 402 receiving yards, which are the third-most in franchise history through the first four games of a season. Defense dominates for 3 quarters, then slips For the first three quarters, Mike Macdonald’s defense had once again completely bottled up Kyler Murray & Co. The Seahawks held Arizona to just six points and 138 total yards through the first 45 minutes on Thursday night, which comes after they limited the Cardinals to just 24 points combined in their two matchups last season. But in the fourth quarter, Murray and the Cardinals caught fire with a pair of touchdown drives that tied the game. Murray led Arizona on an eight-play, 73-yard TD drive that made it a seven-point game with 5:50 to play and then a 12-play, 57-yard TD drive that evened the score in the final minute. Seattle’s defense still did a lot of good things overall, holding the Cardinals to just 253 total yards and 4.0 yards per play, while coming up with two takeaways and six sacks. But the Seahawks’ defense no doubt will be frustrated with its inability to put the game away in the fourth. Emari Demercado! The @AZCardinals have tied this game 💪 SEAvsAZ on Prime Video Also streaming on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Lgt5gQAywX — NFL (@NFL) September 26, 2025 Tight ends have big night With Smith-Njigba quiet for much of the night, Seattle’s tight ends helped fill the void in the passing game. AJ Barner had three catches for 32 yards, including a 16-yard touchdown reception in the first quarter. It was Barner’s second TD of the season and his fifth TD in the past 10 games dating back to last year. Arroyo, meanwhile, had two catches for 44 yards. The rookie second-round draft pick began the Seahawks’ first TD drive with a 12-yard reception and kickstarted their second TD drive with the aforementioned 32-yard leaping catch over edge rusher Josh Sweat. Later in that second TD drive, Arroyo also drew a 16-yard pass interference penalty in the end zone on seven-time Pro Bowl safety Budda Baker, which set up Charbonnet’s scoring run. Blocking tight end Eric Saubert also made a pivotal play on the opening snap of the second half, when he fell on a strip-sack fumble to prevent a turnover that would have gifted the Cardinals a prime scoring opportunity. Sam Darnold goes to AJ Barner for the @Seahawks TD! SEAvsAZ on Prime Video Also streaming on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Psn4OinNbG — NFL (@NFL) September 26, 2025 Run game bounces back Seattle’s rushing attack sputtered for much of the first three weeks, ranking just 21st in the league with 96.0 yards per game and 28th with 3.3 yards per carry. But on Thursday night, the Seahawks’ ground game took a step forward with 155 rushing yards and 4.4 yards per carry. Kenneth Walker III ran for 81 yards on 19 carries, including three straight carries for 38 yards on Seattle’s first touchdown drive. Zach Charbonnet added 39 yards on 12 carries, including a key 15-yard run on a drive that he later capped by bulldozing into the end zone for a 1-yard TD on third-and-goal. There were a handful of runs that went for no gain or negative yardage, so it was still a bit of a hot-and-cold night for the ground game. But overall, it was a nice step forward. Charbonnet powers his way into the endzone to extend @Seahawks lead 💪 SEAvsAZ on Prime Video Also streaming on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/8kMeEQnUi7 — NFL (@NFL) September 26, 2025 Self-inflicted mistakes nearly prove costly For Seattle, this game probably never should have come down to the wire. The Seahawks were in firm control for most of the night and had several prime opportunities to widen their lead. But thanks to some self-inflicted mistakes, they allowed Arizona to hang around and make a late rally. In the first quarter, safety Coby Bryant came up with an interception, but fumbled the ball right back to Arizona after getting hit by teammate Tyrice Knight. The Cardinals capitalized on the extra opportunity by driving for a field goal, which remained their only points until late in the third quarter. Later in the first half, Walker was flagged for a back-breaking 15-yard taunting penalty that backed the Seahawks into a third-and-18 and ultimately pushed them out of field-goal range. Early in the fourth quarter, Smith-Njigba was called for a holding penalty that wiped away a Charbonnet TD run and forced Seattle to settle for a field goal. And later in the fourth, Myers’ missed field goal kept the door open for the Cardinals. Fortunately for the Seahawks, the miscues didn’t end up costing them in the win column. text_body: Presented by Rapid Reaction: Buccaneers 38, Seahawks 35, The Buccaneers defeated the Seahawks 38-35 and improve to 4-1 Oct 05, 2025 at 09:35 PM Brianna Dix Staff Writer/Reporter Copied! The Buccaneers defeated the Seahawks and improve to 4-1 on the season with a 39-yard field goal by Chase McLaughlin as time expired. Lavonte David helped seal the victory with a late interception of Sam Darnold. Baker Mayfield finished the game completing 29 of 33 pass attempts for 379 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions for a 134.7 rating. Emeka Egbuka concluded the game with 163 yards and a touchdown. On the Bucs' opening possession, Cade Otton took advantage of Seattle's zone coverage, sitting in coverage voids and Baker Mayfield connected with the tight end for gains of 27 and 12 yards. The 11-play, 69-yard drive culminated in a Chase McLaughlin 30-yard field goal to give Tampa Bay an early 3-0 start. The Seahawks followed suit with a field goal attempt of their own but Jason Myers' 44-yard attempt was wide left. To open the second frame, the Bucs made their way down the field but after an incompletion to Chris Godwin Jr. on third down, the Bucs were forced to kick a field goal. McLaughlin's 36-yard kick was good, putting Tampa Bay in the driver's seat, 6-0. The Bucs' defense answered with a stout drive, including a tackle for loss by Lavonte David on Zach Charbonnet (-2) and a pass breakup by Antoine Winfield Jr. versus Jaxon Smith-Njigba to stifle Seattle's momentum. On Seattle's following drive, Jalen Milroe fumbled at the Tampa Bay 42-yard line and it was recovered by Tykee Smith at the 41-yard line. Prior to the two-minute mark in the second quarter, Rachaad White found the end zone on a seven-yard touchdown rush to give Tampa Bay a 13-0 lead. Earlier in the drive, Otton accelerated off a chip-and-release for a gain of 17 yards to spur the score. The Seahawks followed with a 10-play, 54-yard scoring drive that culminated in a six-yard touchdown for Jaxon Smith-Njigba. He crossed the back of the end zone and Darnold hit him in stride to make it a 13-7 game prior to the half. Coming out of the half, the Seahawks posted a four-play, 77-yard scoring drive including a 36-yard gain by Dareke Young and a 31-yard run by Kenneth Walker III around the right end, which helped set up the five-yard touchdown rush for Charbonnet around the right tackle. On Tampa Bay's ensuing drive, Tez Johnson became the catalyst, juking defenders to move the chains. The nine-play, 77-yard drive resulted in an Emeka Egbuka 20-yard touchdown. He won with inside leverage and Mayfield placed the ball out in front where only the rookie could snag it. The two-point attempt to Egbuka was successful, providing the Bucs with a 21-14 advantage. The Seahawks answered with a score of their own. Smith-Njigba picked up 53 yards following a deep bomb by Darnold and AJ Barner capped off the drive with a two-yard touchdown, making it a tied game at 21. The shootout continued as the Bucs put seven on the board. Egbuka showcased his savvy route running with a lethal stutter-step mid-route to create separation for a 57-yard gain, making it look like he was going to break inside and instead he continued deep. That play spurred White's one-yard touchdown rush, giving Tampa Bay a 28-21 lead. On Seattle's following drive, an illegal contact penalty against Tampa Bay nullified Antoine Winfield Jr.'s interception and Seattle capitalized with a six-yard touchdown to Barner, tying the game at 28. The Bucs were forced to punt on their next drive following a second-down sack and an incompletion to Sterling Shepard on third down. With just over three minutes in the fourth quarter, the Seahawks capped off an eight-play, 99-yard touchdown drive with a 21-yard Horton score to put Seattle out in front, 35-28. The Bucs responded with a score of their own. 25-yard gains for Otton and Egbuka helped set up the 11-yard score for Sterling Shepard, which tied the game at 35. Lavonte David then intercepted Darnold's pass at the Seattle 38-yard line and returned it three yards. The Bucs won with a walk-off 39-yard field goal by Chase McLaughlin to make it a 38-35 final score at Lumen Field. text_body: SEATTLE SEAHAWKS Stacy: The good and bad of Seahawks’ loss to Bucs in thriller Oct 5, 2025, 5:15 PM | Updated: 5:23 pm Seahawks Re-Sign Rashid Shaheed + Free Agency Departures & News - REACTION Hosts Dave Wyman and Bob Stelton (Wyman & Bob) to discuss the news of the first day of NFL Free agency for the Seattle Seahawks, Including the Seahawks resigning Rashid Shaheed and Josh Jobe. Buccaneers 38, Seahawks 35: Recap | Instant Reaction | Box score Two teams with two stout defenses turned a potential low-scoring affair into a shootout between two quarterbacks who, coincidentally, once spent time on the same roster in Carolina. In the end, it was Baker Mayfield who outdueled his former teammate Sam Darnold. Or was it Darnold who outdueled himself by throwing a late interception ? Or, wait, was the fight lost when Seattle’s defense couldn’t stop the Bucs from returning blow for blow? Turns out a surprising game left some confusing takeaways. Here’s the good and bad of each. Darnold’s stellar outing ended with heartbreak, but should leave you feeling encouraged. Darnold technically didn’t make the pass that mattered most, which I suppose you could say for any pass that’s intercepted with less than a minute remaining from your own 38-yard line. But he made a lot of passes that really mattered, and that’s encouraging for a Seahawks offense that entered the season with the expectation that Darnold would be a lesser version of his 2024 self. Darnold’s final line (28 for 34, 341 yards, four touchdowns, one interception) isn’t going to reflect the bit of luck he got away with in the fourth, nor the brilliance from a few of his shots. A pass nearly tipped for what would’ve been a pick six took another bounce into the air and fell into the waiting arms of Cooper Kupp. There’s some luck for you. But a 53-yarder to a sprinting Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who had a defender on his hip? Evading pressure on fourth down to toss a touchdown to rookie Tory Horton? Those were clutch plays, and there were more from the offense in the second half, and it deserves a fair share of credit even with a loss. Made it look easy. 😤 Darnold to JSN for 53 yards. 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/aPg0aP9s9A — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 5, 2025 That's how you answer on fourth. 😮‍💨 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/I9tppE8WmF — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 5, 2025 It really makes the final pick a shame. “At the end of the day I’ve gotta protect the football in that situation,” Darnold told reporters after the game, doling out credit to the Bucs’ defense. He felt he should’ve changed the protection pre-snap. “That was bad quarterback play on that last snap.” The Bucs were short a few defenders of their own, including a starting and a backup cornerback. They kept a lid on Seattle’s offense through most of the first half but allowed 311 yards from the Seahawks in the second half alone. “Just crushing,” Kupp said of the loss, a line that perfectly summed up the feeling of fans leaving the stadium to waltz next door to T-Mobile Field with prayers that the Mariners could save their season. It’s been a tough weekend for Seattle sports. The Seahawks defense isn’t as bad as their numbers Sunday, but injuries adding up could change that. On to the more confusing and concerning part of the day. The Seahawks were a top scoring defense in the second half of last season. Through four weeks this year they were even better, ranking third in points allowed behind Denver and Houston. They’ve been one of the better defenses against the run and in the red zone this year (46%). That’s a good chunk of time to establish some fairly reliable trends. Sunday might’ve been their worst performance yet under coach Mike Macdonald. Mayfield and the Bucs marched down the field over and over, racking up 426 net yards, 38 points, and going over 60% on both third down and in the red zone. How big a factor are injuries here? The Seahawks entered the day without starting safety Julian Love — a leader on that side of the ball — and starting corner Devon Witherspoon. The defensive line was missing DeMarcus Lawrence. But no matter, the Bucs were without wide receiver Mike Evans and running back Bucky Irving, so all’s fair, right? Easier to say when you’re only short three defenders. The Bucs attacked early, adding just a pair of field goals to start the game but otherwise moving far more easily than previous opponents against this group. By the end of the game the defense was being torched far too frequently. The Bucs didn’t need Irving after all — turns out 56 rushing yards won’t do you in when Mayfield can pass for 370. I don’t think the defense Macdonald rolled out Week 1 is this bad. And we know that — they’ve proven to be a stellar unit so far. But the defense they might have to roll out if these injuries are more concerning? That’s a pretty massive question mark. text_body: Game Report, 2025 Week 6: Seahawks 20, Jaguars 12 Oct 12, 2025 at 04:22 PM John Oehser Jaguars Senior Writer Copied! JACKSONVILLE – The scrap, grit and want-to were there yet again. This time, those weren't enough. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw two touchdowns and the Jaguars inched close late, but what had been reliable wasn't on Sunday – and in a game largely defined by Jaguars mistakes, the Seattle Seahawks held on for a 20-12 victory in front of 61,056 at EverBank Stadium on a sun-splashed October afternoon. "We didn't play our best ball today," Lawrence said. Head Coach Liam Coen called "deflating moments" the "theme of the day." "We will not beat quality teams like this if we continue to hurt ourselves," Coen said. "We continue to hurt ourselves and have these self-inflicted wounds. That ultimately is on me." The Seahawks clinched the victory by kneeling out the final 1:57 on their final drive, with tight end AJ Barner's 61-yard reception from quarterback Sam Darnold giving them possession deep in Jaguars territory. The Jaguars had three possessions in the fourth quarter trailing by eight points – their three series before Seattle's final drive – but produced just one first down on the three drives. "It's on all of us," Lawrence said. "It's all of us taking accountability and fixing the things we can control." After entering Sunday with an NFL-leading 14 takeaways, the Jaguars didn't force one Sunday. The Jaguars, after allowing six sacks in the first five games, allowed seven for 44 yards to the Seahawks. The Seahawks also were credited with 17 hits on Lawrence. "Credit to them: They beat us up up front," Coen said. The Jaguars also were penalized 10 times for 76 yards, with Coen emphasizing that too many of the penalties came at critical times. "We have to look in the mirror and fix the problems that have been there all year," Lawrence said. The Jaguars (4-2) lost after winning three consecutive games, with the Seahawks (4-2) winning for a third time in four games. The Jaguars are 3-1 at EverBank Stadium this season, with Sunday's game extending the Seahawks' road winning streak to nine games. Darnold threw a 61-yard second-quarter touchdown to wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba and an 11-yard third-quarter touchdown to wide receiver Cooper Kupp to give the Seahawks a 20-6 lead entering the fourth quarter. Lawrence gave the Jaguars an early lead with a first-quarter touchdown pass to wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr., then pulled them to within eight points with a touchdown pass to wide receiver Tim Patrick early in the fourth quarter. "Guys fought," cornerback Jourdan Lewis said. "We fought back. It just wasn't good enough." Lawrence completed 27 of 42 passes for 258 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, with running back Travis Etienne Jr. rushing for 27 yards on 12 carries. Brian Thomas Jr. caught eight passes for 90 yards and a touchdown. "Some of the stuff we were doing was working," Thomas said. "We've just got to quit beating ourselves." Darnold completed 16 of 27 passes for 295 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, with running back Kenneth Walker III rushing for 34 yards 10 carries. Smith-Njigba caught eight passes for 162 yards and one touchdown. Jaguars kicker Cam Little missed an extra point and a 50-yard field goal in the first half, with the Seahawks leading 10-6 at halftime. The Jaguars not only did not have a takeaway for the first time this season on Sunday, they registered just one sack – by defensive tackle Arik Armstead when the Jaguars blitzed Darnold. The Seahawks managed just 13 first downs, but 122 of their 346 yards came on two long pass plays – to Smith-Nigba and Barner. "They hit enough explosives and we didn't," Coen said. "That's the reality. We didn't get after their quarterback. They got after ours. They hit a couple of big plays in the pass game and we did not. We have to get after their quarterback more as they got after ours." 2025 Week 6, Step by step: Thomas' 21-yard reception from Lawrence gave the Jaguars a 6-0 lead with 1:14 remaining in the first quarter, capping an eight-play, 61-yard drive on which the Jaguars twice converted third downs of more than 10 yards. The Jaguars outgained the Seahawks, 90-36, in the first quarter. Myers' 24-yard field goal cut the lead to 6-3 with 10:38 remaining in the second quarter, with Darnold's 61-yard touchdown pass to Smith-Njigba on the first play of the Seahawks' ensuing series giving them a 10-6 lead with 8:34 remaining in the first half. Myers' 53-yard field goal gave the Seahawks a 13-6 lead with :10 remaining in a second quarter in which they outgained the Jaguars, 136-62. Kupp's 11-yard reception from Darnold extended the Seahawks' lead to 20-6 with 10:14 remaining in the third quarter. Lawrence's 26-yard touchdown pass to Patrick capped a 14-play, 82-yard drive and cut the lead to 20-12 with 13:00 remaining. Notable: Rookie center Jonah Monheim made his first career start with starter Robert Hainsey inactive after sustaining a hamstring injury in a victory over the Kansas City Chiefs last Monday. The Jaguars' other four inactive players Sunday: Running back Cody Schrader, defensive tackle Khalen Saunders Sr., linebacker Yasir Abdullah and safety Kahlef Hailassie. Abdullah missed a third consecutive game with a hamstring injury, with defensive end Travon Walker returning after missing the Chiefs game with a wrist injury. Jaguars rookie guard Wyatt Milum and rookie defensive end Danny Striggow were active for the first time this season, with Milum missing the first five games with a knee injury. Also: cornerback Greg Newsome II – acquired in a trade from the Cleveland Browns on Thursday – was active and played in a reserve role. Injury report: The Jaguars reported no significant injuries Sunday. Seattle Seahawks 20, Jacksonville Jaguars 12: Box Score | Recap The defense piled up seven sacks in a bounce-back win for the Seahawks, who lost Florida’s other team, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, in a shootout at home last weekend. Seattle improved to 4-2 with its Week 6 triumph and moved into a three-way tie for first place in the NFC West. Stacy Rost: 3 nuggets from short-handed Seattle Seahawks’ win over Jags Here are the instant reactions to Sunday’s game from some of the voices of Seattle Sports, including Seahawks Radio Network analyst Dave Wyman’s thoughts in the video the at the top of this post. Bob Stelton – Wyman & Bob (2-7 p.m. weekdays) This is a very nice win on the road for the Seattle Seahawks. Jacksonville has been a surprise team coming in with a 4-1 record and, despite being riddled with injuries on defense, the Hawks held the Jags to just 12 points and sacked Trevor Lawrence seven times! Lawrence had only been sacked a total of six times in five games coming into this one. Kudos to Byron Murphy II, who had two sacks on the day and now has 4 1/2 on the season. He had just one-half sack all of last season. Also, a very nice return to the field for Demarcus Lawrence chipping in with 2 1/2 sacks on the day. Another stellar day for Sam Darnold going 16 of 27 for 295 yards and two touchdowns. It was almost a 50-50 split between run and pass on the day – 27 pass attempts to 26 run attempts. Really the only negative offensively was their inability to get that run game going, coming away with just 60 total yards on those 26 carries. Other than that, there’s a lot to be excited about on a day where this team went on the road very short-handed on defense and beat a team that has been rolling. Watch out for Byron 👀 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/LaMVqmmXjs — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 Brock Huard – Brock & Salk (6-10 a.m. weekdays) View this post on Instagram A post shared by Seattle Sports (@seattlesports710) Mike Lefko – Wyman & Bob Game ball to the Seattle Seahawks’ defensive line for setting the tone early and stepping up to help a secondary dealing with injury attrition. Trevor Lawrence had only been sacked six times total in five games coming into this one, but the Seahawks defensive front got to him early and helped rack up a season-high seven on the day. Sam Darnold has continued to play like one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL. His feathery throw to Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a 61-yard TD flipped momentum early in the game, and he made one of the biggest plays of the day with his third-down touchdown strike to Cooper Kupp. The Seahawks’ lack of a run game made for another adventure when trying to close out a game again. They couldn’t hold a lead against the Cardinals, and this one became a little too close for comfort today. For as good as Darnold has been, it becomes very difficult to take significant chunks of time off the clock when your offense is one-dimensional. After one-third of the season, the absence of a sustained rushing attack looms as the biggest issue for the Seahawks’ offense. On the other side of the ball, you hope that an extra day before the Monday night game against the Texans and then a bye week after are the balm for all the injuries ailing your key players in the secondary. (AP) — Having thrown a combined six interceptions in his last two starts in Jacksonville, Sam Darnold refused to get greedy this time around. Seattle Seahawks 20, Jacksonville Jaguars 12: Box Score He played it safe and ended up with a turnover-free performance. Darnold threw for 295 yards, with touchdown passes to Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp , and the Seattle Seahawks dominated both lines of scrimmage on their way to a 20-12 victory against the Jaguars on Sunday. “I told myself I was going to take what they give me, and if they give me a checkdown, take it,” said Darnold, whose late interception last week proved costly against Tampa Bay. “I felt like I did a pretty good job of that.” Smith-Njigba finished with eight catches for 162 yards as the Seahawks (4-2) rebounded from a last-second loss to the Buccaneers and improved to 22-6 over the last decade in 1 p.m. kickoffs on the East Coast. The Jaguars (4-2), meanwhile, looked every bit like a team that spent the week reveling in a Monday night victory against three-time AFC champion Kansas City. Jacksonville’s first three snaps set the tone: a sack, a holding penalty and a 3-yard loss. The Jags were penalized 10 times for 76 yards. Trevor Lawrence was sacked a season-high seven times. Travis Etienne was held to 27 yards on 12 carries. Brian Thomas Jr. dropped a third-down pass late with no defenders on him. And the Jaguars had a 54-yard TD pass from Lawrence to Thomas nullified because rookie Travis Hunter lined up offsides. “It’s an undisciplined operation at the moment,” coach Liam Coen said. “What’s standing in our way? Right now, it’s us.” . @TankLawrence came through SWINGING. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/wjR4kfb1mR — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 Jacksonville still made it close in the fourth quarter following Lawrence’s 26-yard TD pass to Tim Patrick. It helped that Seattle went 1 for 11 on third downs. But the Seahawks sealed it by forcing three punts in the fourth and then Darnold connected with tight end AJ Barner for a 61-yarder , which allowed them to run out the clock after another penalty on Jacksonville. He made that look wayyy too easy. 🔥 @_ajbarner_ for 61 yards. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/VCEt8fCDPi — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 “We obviously didn’t play our best ball,” Lawrence said. “A lot of mistakes. A lot of self-inflicted wounds like we’ve talked about in the past. We’ve got to clean it up.” It was the first time this season that the Jaguars failed to notch a takeaway. They entered the week leading the league with 14. “That was critical,” Seattle coach Mike Macdonald said. “We knew they would do that going into the game. They’re an opportunistic team. The numbers speak for themselves. I thought our ball security was tremendous.” Newsome burned on his first snap with Jacksonville Newly acquired Jaguars cornerback Greg Newsome made a less-than-ideal first impression. Smith-Njigba torched Newsome for a 61-yard TD reception on Newsome’s first snap with Jacksonville. “I knew (Newsome was in the game),” Smith-Njigba said. “But that was good to take advantage of that look and execute.” The Jaguars traded cornerback Tyson Campbell for Newsome on Wednesday night. Someone hit rewind. 61-yards to the end zone. 🔥 @jaxon_smith1 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/K2SywHB46G — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 Wesley Hines-Allen serves as an honorary captain Jaguars defensive end and team captain Josh Hines-Allen had a special helper for the coin toss. Hines-Allen brought his 8-year-old son, Wesley, to midfield as part of the NFL’s “Crucial Catch” program, which is dedicated to fighting cancer and saving lives. Wesley was an honorary captain two months after completing treatment for pediatric cancer. Wesley was diagnosed with acute promyelocytic leukemia in December and underwent chemotherapy for six months. Key injuries Seattle Seahawks: DT Jarran Reed injured his left leg in the fourth quarter. The Seahawks played without three starting defensive backs: S Julian Love and CBs Devon Witherspoon and CB Tariq Woolen. Jaguars: LB Devin Lloyd felt “a little tight,” but the team never reported an injury and later said he was on the bench because of a coaches’ decision. DE Travon Walker was active less than two weeks after having wrist surgery. He played mostly on passing downs while wearing a club on his left hand. Up next The Seahawks stay in the AFC South and host Houston next Monday night. The Jaguars “host” the Los Angeles Rams at Wembley Stadium in London next Sunday. text_body: SEATTLE SEAHAWKS Observations from Seahawks’ 20-12 win over Jaguars Oct 12, 2025, 2:30 PM | Updated: 9:57 pm Seahawks Re-Sign Rashid Shaheed + Free Agency Departures & News - REACTION Hosts Dave Wyman and Bob Stelton (Wyman & Bob) to discuss the news of the first day of NFL Free agency for the Seattle Seahawks, Including the Seahawks resigning Rashid Shaheed and Josh Jobe. They were coming off a difficult last-second loss the week prior. And they were traveling some 2,400 miles across the country to face a surging 4-1 team in a game that kicked off at 10 a.m. Pacific time. No problem. The Seahawks simply did what they’ve done so often under second-year head coach Mike Macdonald – win on the road. Instant reaction | Recap | Box score Seattle beat the Jacksonville Jaguars 20-12 on Sunday to improve to 4-2 on the season. It was the Seahawks’ ninth straight road victory and it improved them to 10-1 on the road under Macdonald. Here are three things that stood out from Seattle’s latest triumph away from home. JSN continues his tear By this point, it’s become clear. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has emerged as one of the league’s top wide receivers. The third-year Seattle wideout had another monster game, recording eight catches for 162 yards and a touchdown – including five catches for 117 yards and a TD by the midway point of the second quarter. It bumped Smith-Njigba’s season total to 696 receiving yards, which is the 15th-most by any NFL player through his team’s first six games since the 1970 NFL merger, according to Stathead . Smith-Njigba’s biggest play came on a 61-yard TD catch midway through the second quarter, when he raced past newly acquired cornerback Greg Newsome II and hauled in a perfectly placed deep ball from Sam Darnold for the longest reception of his career. Smith-Njigba also had catches of 35 and 32 yards, which gives him an NFL-high eight receptions of 30-plus yards this season. Touchdown JSN! 61 yards. SEAvsJAX on FOX/FOX One https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/2RqhCoOuX4 — NFL (@NFL) October 12, 2025 Seattle’s pass rush takes over With the Seahawks down three key players in their secondary – two-time Pro Bowl cornerback Devon Witherspoon, veteran safety Julian Love and cornerback Riq Woolen – they needed a bounceback performance up front after mustering only one sack in last week’s 38-35 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The pass rush delivered in a massive way. Seattle applied constant pressure on Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence and piled up a season-high seven sacks – which was especially impressive considering the Jaguars had allowed just six sacks through their first five games. DeMarcus Lawrence and Byron Murphy II led the way with 2.0 sacks apiece, Uchenna Nwosu recorded 1.5 sacks, linebacker Drake Thomas added a sack on a blitz and Leonard Williams was credited with a half-sack. . @TankLawrence came through SWINGING. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/wjR4kfb1mR — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 Moreover, two of the sacks came in particularly pivotal moments. Late in the first half, DeMarcus Lawrence took down Trevor Lawrence for a 9-yard loss that created a longer field-goal attempt for Jacksonville kicker Cam Little, who then sailed his ensuing 50-yard attempt wide of the right upright. And with the Seahawks holding an eight-point lead with less than 4 minutes left in the game, Lawrence and Nwosu combined for a third-down sack that forced Jacksonville to punt. The Jaguars never got the ball back after that. Hawks close it out For as well as the Seahawks have played this season, they’ve had issues closing out games. In their Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, they blew a late four-point lead by surrendering a go-ahead TD drive in the closing minutes. In last week’s loss to the Buccaneers, they blew a late seven-point lead by giving up a game-tying TD drive and then handing the ball right back to Tampa Bay on a costly interception that set up the Bucs’ game-winning field goal. And in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals, they blew a 14-point fourth-quarter lead before rebounding to win on a last-second kick. For a moment, Sunday’s game was in danger of following a similar script. After taking a 20-6 lead into the fourth quarter, the Seahawks surrendered a 14-play, 82-yard TD drive and then gave the ball right back to Jacksonville following a three-and-out by their offense. Suddenly, the Jaguars had the ball with a chance to mount a game-tying TD drive. But this time, the Seahawks closed it out. Seattle’s defense stymied the Jaguars the rest of the way, holding them to just 17 yards combined over their final three possessions. Darnold then provided the knockout punch, connecting with wide-open tight end AJ Barner for a 61-yard completion that ultimately sealed the victory. AJ Barner in open space for 61 yards! This was also a Jags team that was leading the league in turnover differential (plus-eight) with at least three takeaways in four games this year. Sam Darnold couldn’t throw a pick or fumble, backups in the secondary would be tasked with holding back Jags leading receiver Brian Thomas Jr. (Seattle has lost both games in which they’ve allowed a 100-plus-yard receiver) and would need to get their run game going against a good run defense. Instant Reaction: Seattle Seahawks secure 20-12 road win over Jags The result? Seattle didn’t turn the ball over once, saw an explosive day from Darold and Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and bounced back from a Week 5 loss with a win. Here are some extra nuggets from a Week 6 victory. JSN finally gets a win to go with a top performance Smith-Njigba is on pace to smash DK Metcalf’s franchise record for single-season receiving yards. He’s already got more yards through the first six weeks than Metcalf did to begin any season with Seattle, though that’s a credit to Smith-Njigba and not a knock on a spectacular Seahawks career for No. 14. But Sunday’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars also broke an unlucky trend for JSN: his three best single-game performances had all come with losses. That includes 180 yards against the Rams last season (a 26-20 loss in overtime), 132 yards in a 38-35 loss to the Buccaneers last week, and 124 yards to open the season against San Francisco. JSN’s 162 yards in Week 6 are the second-most in any game of his career and the first of over 124 yards to come with a win. Someone hit rewind. 61-yards to the end zone. 🔥 @jaxon_smith1 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/K2SywHB46G — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 Darnold remains the league’s most explosive passer Who’d have thought we’d be saying this? Anyone hoping the Seahawks would get a game manager has gotten more than they could’ve dreamed with Darnold’s 2025 campaign so far. Observations from Seahawks’ 20-12 win over Jaguars Entering this game, Darnold and Indianapolis quarterback Daniel Jones (!) were tied for the most passing plays of 40 or more yards. Both quarterbacks’ teams won today, but Darnold was the only of the two to add on to that explosive-pass-play total. Jones’ longest play of the day was a 26-yarder to Alec Pierce. Darnold had two 61-yard completions against a Jags defense that ranks 27th against the pass, and one of them was a touchdown. Both passes being 61 yards also adds a fun twist on a trend through six games: Darnold’s longest pass completion each and every week has been to Smith-Njigba, but the Ohio State product isn’t in sole possession of that title this week since tight end AJ Barner also snagged one of those two . He made that look wayyy too easy. 🔥 @_ajbarner_ for 61 yards. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/VCEt8fCDPi — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 12, 2025 A Seahawks defense under pressure brings some of its own The Seahawks entered Sunday short three starting defensive backs, including their leader in the secondary in safety Jordan Love. Communication issues popped up on one Jacksonville scoring drive in particular. Busted coverage. Jags score. With arms wiiide open! @BrianThomas_11 | 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/Q9MfrWAOhr — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) October 12, 2025 But the defense didn’t just tighten up; they also continued to bring pressure for a season-high seven sacks (their previous high: six against the Cardinals in Week 4). It continues an impressive effort by the Seahawks’ defense to get sacks without blitzing nearly as much as other teams, and to rack up pressures without having a top player in that category. Byron Murphy II had the most of any Seahawk with nine total pressures through five weeks, well outside players in the top 10 who all have 12 or more. Who do you persistently double team when you’re not quiet sure who could lead the team that day? It’s a bad problem for opposing offenses and a boon for Seattle so far.
